I specialize in developing machine learning and probabilistic tools for analyzing bioacoustic data, with applications to threatened species conservation and landscape-scale ecological monitoring.

title: Research
text:
Current Projects

Bioacoustic Monitoring of Threatened Species
Northern Spotted Owl Population Dynamics
Developing integrated approaches combining historical territory data with passive acoustic monitoring to assess population trends and occupancy patterns of this federally threatened species.
Marbled Murrelet Forest Habitat Use
Using convolutional neural networks and passive acoustic recorders to facilitate near real-time monitoring of marbled murrelets across forested landscapes, enabling better understanding of terrestrial habitat requirements.


Machine Learning for Bioacoustics
Audio Classification Under Data Scarcity
Developing simulated soundscape approaches to improve acoustic classifier performance when training data is limited, with applications to rare species detection.
Individual Identification in Acoustic Recordings
Contributing to advancing methods for individual animal identification using acoustic signatures, with implications for demographic studies and population monitoring.


Bayesian Statistical Methods
Multi-state Occupancy Modeling
Developing methods to integrate long-term monitoring data across different survey methodologies, addressing spatial mismatch and methodological transitions in wildlife monitoring programs.
Mark-Recapture Analysis
Investigating emigration effects on survival estimates and developing improved analytical approaches for small mammal demographic studies.

title: Research
text:
Research Themes

1. Conservation Technology

Passive Acoustic Monitoring: Deploying automated recording systems for continuous wildlife monitoring
Machine Learning Applications: Developing AI tools for species detection and behavior classification
Remote Sensing Integration: Combining acoustic data with satellite and LiDAR data for landscape-scale analysis



2. Population Ecology

Demographic Modeling: Understanding vital rates and population dynamics of threatened species
Occupancy Analysis: Assessing species distribution patterns and habitat relationships
Survival Analysis: Investigating factors affecting wildlife survival and reproduction



3. Landscape Ecology

Habitat Fragmentation: Examining effects of forest management on wildlife populations
Multi-scale Analysis: Connecting local habitat features to landscape-scale patterns
Climate Change Impacts: Assessing species responses to environmental change

title: Research
text:
International Collaborations

African Wildlife Conservation
Collaborating on wildlife monitoring projects in Malawi’s Nkhotakota Wildlife Reserve, including: - African elephant abundance estimation - Large mammal population assessments - Passive acoustic monitoring pilot studies


Global Soundscape Analysis
Contributing to worldwide syntheses of passive acoustic monitoring across terrestrial and aquatic realms, advancing our understanding of global biodiversity patterns.

title: Research
text:
Methodological Innovations

Statistical Methods

Bayesian Hierarchical Models: Advanced modeling frameworks for complex ecological data
Multi-species Analysis: Developing methods to analyze community-level responses
Uncertainty Quantification: Incorporating multiple sources of uncertainty in ecological predictions



Technology Development

Automated Detection Algorithms: Creating species-specific detection systems
Data Processing Pipelines: Developing efficient workflows for large-scale acoustic data analysis
Quality Control Methods: Establishing protocols for acoustic data validation and error assessment

title: Research
text:
Future Directions
My research continues to evolve at the intersection of ecology, technology, and conservation, with ongoing work focusing on:

Real-time Monitoring Systems: Developing near real-time species detection capabilities
Multi-sensor Integration: Combining acoustic, visual, and environmental sensors
Predictive Modeling: Using machine learning for forecasting species responses to environmental change
Open Science Tools: Contributing to open-source software for bioacoustic analysis


For detailed methodology and results, see my Publications page.

title: Matthew J. Weldy, PhD Candidate
text:
Matthew J. Weldy, PhD Candidate
Forest Ecosystems and Society at Oregon State University
I am a wildlife ecologist and data scientist specializing in bioacoustics, machine learning, and conservation biology. Currently pursuing my PhD at Oregon State University, I work at the intersection of technology and wildlife conservation to develop innovative solutions for monitoring and protecting threatened species.
My research leverages machine learning and probabilistic tools to process and analyze bioacoustics data for wildlife conservation and ecosystem monitoring. My technical expertise spans Bayesian modeling, spatial analysis, and field ecology, with a focus on developing practical tools for conservation practitioners.
Learn more about me →

Currently based in Port Townsend, Washington, conducting field research throughout the Pacific Northwest and collaborating with research teams across North America and internationally.

title: About
text:
I am a wildlife ecologist and data scientist specializing in bioacoustics, machine learning, and conservation biology. Currently pursuing my PhD in Forest Ecosystems and Society at Oregon State University, I work at the intersection of technology and wildlife conservation to develop innovative solutions for monitoring and protecting threatened species.
My research leverages machine learning and probabilistic tools to process and analyze bioacoustics data for wildlife conservation and ecosystem monitoring. I work with Dr. Matthew G. Betts and Dr. Damon B. Lesmeister to develop practical tools that help conservation practitioners make data-driven decisions.

title: About
text:
Background
I received my Master of Science in Wildlife Science from Oregon State University in 2018, where I studied spatiotemporal associations of abundance and vital rates of co-occurring small mammals in late successional forests. Prior to that, I earned a Bachelor of Science in Plant Biology from the University of Minnesota and a Geographic Information Systems Certificate from California State University, Fresno.

title: About
text:
Technical Expertise
My technical skills span programming languages (R, Python, Julia), machine learning frameworks (PyTorch, Keras, TensorFlow, Jax), and statistical modeling (Bayesian modeling, mark-recapture analysis, occupancy modeling). I also have extensive experience in spatial analysis using ArcGIS and QGIS, as well as field techniques including bioacoustics monitoring, wildlife trapping, and habitat assessment.

title: About
text:
Current Work
I currently work as a Research Fellow with the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education at the USDA Forest Service, Pacific Northwest Research Station. My work focuses on developing machine learning approaches for bioacoustics analysis and conducting Bayesian analysis of mark-recapture and occupancy data to support research collaborations.

title: About
text:
Location
I am currently based in Port Townsend, Washington, conducting field research throughout the Pacific Northwest and collaborating with research teams across North America and internationally.
